payload.feature:
LANDING PR #417: make mutation testing structural. Adopt cargo-mutants, baseline core and protocol's refusal paths, and report on every PR (issue #289).

Branch story-289-mutation-testing: one commit, a2c2b360, on main 155aa5f0, from the operator's controller.

Changes:
- .cargo/mutants.toml;
- scripts/mutants.sh, which holds the scope and compares misses with the committed allow-lists by file and mutation;
- quality/mutants/, holding the core and protocol allow-lists and a README with the baseline;
- .github/workflows/mutants.yml, a non-required workflow: --in-diff on PRs and eight weekly shards. Both only report misses, but they fail on a tool error, a red tree, or a missing allow-list or output;
- workflow_pins judges the new workflow;
- tests/support/env_guard.rs's walk gains a positive control (#413's residual).

Judge:
1. Whether the report-only job truly cannot pass when it didn't measure. Look for an empty diff that means "no mutants", a missing output read as "no misses", and a shard that ran nothing.
2. Whether identifying a miss by file and mutation, without the line, can hide a new miss behind an old one.
3. Whether the positive control now binds the guard walk.
4. Whether every action and tool is pinned.

The proposed gate, and which misses to fix first, are for the operator to rule; they are not findings. Seats cannot run cargo-mutants, so judge by reading. If a finding needs a mutants run, rule it residual with the exact patch for the controller.

Local exact coverage on this host misses crates/brokkr-cli/src/ui.rs:1024 on main as well, a host-dependent HOME branch; CI is unaffected. That is not a finding against this PR.

This run lands one pull request under decision 0051 so the contribution gate can vouch for it. If a finding returns the branch, fix exactly that finding, prove any code or test change with a test bound by a compiling mutation, commit one signed-off commit ending "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>", and never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. A new function stays within
  cyclomatic complexity 15, and an existing one never grows more complex.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{
  "repository": "feedback-loop-ai/brokkr",
  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",
  "documentation": ["README.md", "ARCHITECTURE.md", "CONTRIBUTING.md", "docs/guides/", "packaging/README.md"],
  "validation": [

    {"name": "clippy", "command": "cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings"},
    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
    {"name": "release binary", "command": "cargo build --release --locked -p brokkr-cli"},
    {"name": "remote CI", "instructions": "Before tagging, require all applicable CI jobs on the final candidate commit, including both supported operating systems, MSRV, licenses, audit, packaging and exact coverage."}
  ],
  "organization_profiles": [
    {"repository": "feedback-loop-ai/.github", "path": "profile/README.md", "project_url": "https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr", "apply": "after verified publication"}
  ],
  "channels": [
    {"name": "GitHub release", "evidence": "Four platform archives, Linux deb/rpm packages, SHA256SUMS and signed build provenance."},
    {"name": "crates.io", "evidence": "All seven workspace crates serve the new version."},
```

members.adversarial:
Adversarial, read-only review of a2c2b360 (#289 / PR #417). I did not run cargo-mutants; its behaviour is read from the vendored 27.1.0 source in ~/.cargo/registry. I ran cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test workflow_pins (7/7 pass) and simulated the script's own identity/report functions on the committed allow-lists. I judge by concrete inputs -> wrong output.

F1 MEDIUM (judge 2; ruling 9). A miss's identity is file+mutation with no line (scripts/mutants.sh:70), and report() subtracts the run's identities from the whole-scope allow-list with a multiset comm (:84). Both CI modes measure a SUBSET - in-diff mutates only changed lines, a weekly shard ~1/8 of the scope - while known is the whole baseline. So a genuinely new miss whose (file, function, operator) already appears in an allow-list is cancelled by an entry the run never mutated. Reproduced with the script's own functions: a run holding only 'crates/brokkr-core/src/fold.rs:512:9: replace == with != in apply' prints 'Mutants no committed miss names: 0' because 'fold.rs:384:41 replace == with != in apply' is allow-listed; the same for a new 'hands.rs ... replace == with != in box_argv' (three allowed twins at 638/645/652) and 'secret.rs ... replace < with <= in validate_value'. All 13 baselined (file, function, mutation) identities, including every refusal-path function under watch, are blind this way on PRs; it becomes a fail-open the day the operator rules a gate on this comparison. Patch: in-diff lists every miss and annotates an identity match as 'committed miss - check the line' instead of subtracting; for shards, add a final job that downloads the eight artifacts, unions missed.txt and reports once over the whole scope.

F2 MEDIUM (judge 1). measure() treats cargo-mutants' --in-diff no-mutants early exit as a failed measurement. in_diff.rs maps EmptyDiff/NoSourceFiles/NoMutants to ExitCode::Success, and main.rs returns before OutputDir::new, so a diff with no in-scope mutant exits 0 and writes nothing. On a fresh tree measure() then sees status 0 with no missed.txt and exits 1, so the report-only job is red on every PR whose diff has no mutable core/protocol line - this PR included (its only changed .rs files are tests/support/env_guard.rs and crates/brokkr-cli/tests/workflow_pins.rs, both excluded by .cargo/mutants.toml). On a tree that still holds a prior mutants.out, the same early exit leaves the old missed.txt, which measure/report read as this run's result: the report passes green having measured nothing (local hazard; the correctness seat notes CI's rust-cache prunes target/mutants). The commit's stub-cargo control covered 'status 2 with no output', never 'status 0 with no output', which is the tool's real no-mutants path. Patch: rm -rf "$out/mutants.out" before every measure(), and in in-diff run `cargo mutants --list --in-diff ...` first: exit 0 with empty stdout means zero mutants, print a '0 mutants in this diff' summary and exit 0; otherwise measure as today.

F3 LOW (judge 1). A shard that ran nothing passes green. cargo-mutants calls OutputDir::new before test_mutants, and OutputDir::new unconditionally creates missed.txt/caught.txt/...; an empty mutant list logs 'No mutants found' and LabOutcome::new (0/0/0) returns Success. So a shard whose --file scope matches nothing (hands.rs or secret.rs renamed/split) or whose slice is empty reports 0 and exits 0. Separately exit 3 (timeouts) is accepted and timeout.txt is never shown, although the README records timeouts hiding three real protocol misses; and with --baseline=skip the configured timeout_multiplier = 3.0 is inert (timeouts.rs falls back to a fixed 300 s). Patch: fail baseline/shard when outcomes.json total_mutants is 0, and print the timeout/unviable counts beside the fresh misses.

F4 MEDIUM (judge 3; ruling 9). The new positive control binds the traversal but not the walk applying the matcher. Deleting the one line tests/support/env_guard.rs:181 'writers_in(root, &name, offenders);' compiles (writers_in is still used at :135; offenders by the symlink arm and the final assert) and the test still passes: read = 183 >= READ_FLOOR, both known files present, own = 3 >= 2 from the direct call at :135, offenders empty. A later raw std::env::set_var/remove_var anywhere then goes unreported - the refusal the walk exists to make. Also own.len() >= 2 is met by the matcher's own source literal at :191, so dropping either 'set_var' or 'remove_var' from the matcher word list still passes; and the 'Rust files only' loop at :125-127 is tautological because read is only pushed inside the .rs arm. Patch: count the files writers_under hands to writers_in and assert that count equals read.len(), and assert own against the guard's own two write lines (or a matcher-derived count), then record deleting :181 as a failing control.

F5 INFO. scope_args() (:44-50) reads scope() through a process substitution and never checks its status, so 'scripts/mutants.sh baseline <unknown>' prints 'outside the measured scope', continues with an empty args array, and runs cargo mutants with no --package/--file filter over the whole workspace, writing quality/mutants/<unknown>.missed.txt (I verified the status swallowing in isolation).

F6 INFO. in-diff (:105) passes --package brokkr-core --package brokkr-protocol without scope()'s --file, so it mutates every changed line of brokkr-protocol, past the declared secret.rs/hands.rs scope (over-reporting only). None of the cargo-mutants invocations add --cargo-arg=--locked, so mutant builds float off Cargo.lock.

Judge 4 (pins): clean. workflow_pins runs 7/7 green and lists .github/workflows, so mutants.yml is judged. Every uses: is a 40-hex commit with its release comment (checkout v4.4.0, dtolnay/rust-toolchain, rust-cache v2.9.2, install-action v2.87.20, upload-artifact v4.6.2); toolchain 1.98.0 matches rust-toolchain.toml; cargo-mutants@27.1.0 is an exact release; the two new bubblewrap sites are counted.

No high/critical: every change is report-only tooling or test support, so no product fail-open path or refusal is weakened. The proposed gate and which misses to fix first are the operator's to rule, and the host-dependent ui.rs:1024 coverage gap is not this PR's - neither is a finding.
members.correctness:
Correctness review of a2c2b360 (read-only; the cargo-mutants 27.1.0 installed on the host was run only for its no-build early exits, outputs in a deleted scratch dir).

F1 MEDIUM (Q1; framing/fit, ruling 9 for the stub test that missed it). The in-diff job fails on every PR whose diff has no mutable line in brokkr-core or brokkr-protocol, this PR included. Measured: `cargo mutants --in-diff <empty diff>` prints 'INFO Diff file is empty', and `--in-diff $(git diff 155aa5f0...HEAD) --package brokkr-core --package brokkr-protocol` prints 'INFO No mutants to filter'. Both exit 0 and create no output dir. measure() then reads status 0 as a measurement, finds no missed.txt, and exits 1 ('missed.txt is missing'). This fails closed, not open, but a report-only job that is red on most PRs is not what the framing describes. The stub-cargo control tested status 2 with no output, never status 0 with no output, which is the tool's real no-mutants path. The same early exit also leaves any stale $out/mutants.out/missed.txt in place, and measure() would report it as this run's (a local hazard; rust-cache prunes target/mutants on CI). Patch: in measure(), `rm -rf "$out/mutants.out"` before the run. In in-diff, first run `cargo mutants --list --in-diff "$out/branch.diff" <scope args>`: exit 0 with empty stdout means 0 mutants, so print '### 0 mutants in this diff' and exit 0; otherwise measure and require missed.txt as now. Add that stub case (status 0, no output, empty list) to the recorded controls.

F2 LOW (Q2). A miss's identity without the line can hide a new miss behind an old one. comm -23 counts duplicates, so the hiding needs the run to carry no more copies of an identity than the allow-lists do. In in-diff and shard runs, every allow-list entry the run did not mutate is spare capacity. Example: hands.rs has 3 x 'replace == with != in box_argv' (lines 638, 645 and 652). A PR that adds a fourth, missed `==` in box_argv yields one run miss with that identity against 3 known, and it is silently absorbed. The baseline already collides: `ids` at :673 and its cfg(not(unix)) twin at :678 share three identities, and 0063 removes :678. Patch: in-diff mutates only changed lines, so a shifted-but-unchanged miss never appears there; report every in-diff miss and mark the ones whose exact file:line:col line is allow-listed. In shard mode, first cut `known` to the identities `cargo mutants --list --shard k/8 <scope>` selects, then comm.

F3 MEDIUM (Q3, ruling 9: part of the new control cannot fail). The positive control binds enumeration (floor, .rs-only, two known files) and the matcher (own >= 2) separately, not their composition. `read.push(name)` sits beside `writers_in(root, &name, offenders)` in writers_under. Deleting the writers_in call still compiles, and the test stays green: read is full, own comes from a direct call, and offenders stays empty. The walk then checks no file, which is the exact removal #413's residual asked to bind. Patch: have writers_in take `read: &mut Vec<PathBuf>` and push `name.to_path_buf()` after read_to_string succeeds; the own-control passes a throwaway Vec. Removal control: delete the writers_in call in writers_under, and the test must fail 'the walk read 0 Rust files, under its floor of 120'.

F4 LOW (Q1; ruling 5). Timeouts are neither measured nor reported. measure() treats exit 3 as a measurement, and report() reads only missed.txt, never timeout.txt. The README records that 3 of protocol's 22 timeouts were hidden misses. Shards run --baseline=skip with no --timeout, so cargo-mutants falls back to its 300 s default and ignores timeout_multiplier (the binary carries the 'explicit timeout is recommended when using --baseline=skip' warning). Patch: print timeout.txt identities in the summary, compared with a committed list of the 9 real hangs, and pass an explicit --timeout in shard mode.

F5 LOW (ruling 5). The in-diff arm restates the scope as '--package brokkr-core --package brokkr-protocol' without scope()'s --file limits, so it mutates changed lines in every protocol file (the 1,907 unmeasured). The script's header calls scope() the scope's one home. If the wider PR scope is intended, name it there; otherwise build in-diff's args with scope_args.

Q4 pins: clean. Every uses: is SHA-pinned and matches ci.yml's pins. Toolchain 1.98.0 matches rust-toolchain.toml. cargo-mutants@27.1.0 comes through the pinned install-action. workflow_pins walks .github/workflows, so it judges mutants.yml. Weekly shards: ~733 mutants over 8 fixed-order shards cannot be empty, and the unmutated-green pre-step runs with boundary evidence required. No security residual: every issue above fails closed or only makes the report-only summary incomplete.

result.notes:
Review chief on a2c2b360 (PR #417, #289). Panel: correctness=residual, adversarial=residual, joined result residual at medium; the floor is residual. Neither position's prose addressed the gate or argued for a result, so nothing to rule against. I read the whole diff (scripts/mutants.sh, .github/workflows/mutants.yml, .cargo/mutants.toml, quality/mutants/*, tests/support/env_guard.rs, workflow_pins.rs) and checked each claim against the installed cargo-mutants 27.1.0 in a scratch dir under .forge (removed; tree clean). I changed no files.

SURVIVING FINDINGS (deduplicated; both positions raised R1-R3 and R5):

R1 MEDIUM (judge 1) [correctness F1, adversarial F2]. The in-diff mode cannot tell 'nothing to mutate' from 'tool wrote nothing', and a stale mutants.out passes as this run's. RESIDUALS, all low, none a return:

R1 [low, Judge 1, mine; folds adversarial F2 + correctness I2 (timeout fallback) and adversarial F3 (package list's second home)]. Weekly shards pass --baseline=skip, so nothing proves that cargo-mutants' COPY of the tree under TMPDIR builds and is green: the workflow's 'unmutated scope is green' step proves the checkout, not the copy (the copy respects .gitignore and is built without the checkout's target). A red copy makes every mutant 'caught' and an unbuildable copy makes every mutant 'unviable'; both pass with zero misses. Stub proof: a shard whose mutants.json is non-empty but whose caught, missed and timeout files are all empty exits 0; the same output on the in-diff path prints 'Mutants missed in this diff: 0' and exits 0. Skipping the baseline also leaves .cargo/mutants.toml's timeout_multiplier inert (cargo-mutants falls back to a fixed 300 s test timeout with a warning) while the README's Tools line implies it governs weekly runs, and it is the only reason the package list is written a second time in mutants.yml (ruling 5).
